To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ferroelectricity of materials plays an important role in charge separation and transportation, and thus influences the photocatalytic water splitting efficiency.
the ferroelectric materials have a significant influence on photocatalyst and photoelectrode heterostructures for PC and PEC hydrogen production.

the ferroelectric materials can be used as an effective tool to control the interfacial electronic structures of heterogeneous photocatalyst system, which can be utilized to improve the charge separation and transportation for efficient photocatalytic and/or photoelectrochemical processes.

the implementation of ferroelectric polarization to photocatalytic and PEC water-splitting systems to improve the photocatalytic activity and PEC efficiency.
the implementation of ferroelectric material in photocatalytic (water splitting) and photoelectrocatalytic (water oxidation) reactions.
the implementation of ferroelectric polarization in the photocatalytic and the photoelectrochemical processes of water splitting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ferroelectric materials are a promising class of materials to be utilized in PC and PEC systems for efficient water splitting.
ferroelectrics are promising candidates for the development of advanced heterogeneous photocatalysts for clean energy generation.
ferroelectric materials have great potential to improve the efficiency of PC and PPEC water splitting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polarization in the ferroelectric material can be utilized for the charge separation, which can be used for the photocatalysis and photoelectrolysis of water.
the ferroelectric materials have been implemented in photocatalytic (and photoelectrochemical) water splitting.
ferroelectric materials are promising for photocatalytic and electrocatalytic applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ferroelectric materials can be used in the photocatalyst heterojunctions to achieve efficient charge separation by modulating the space charge region, which is a key step for improving the photocatalytic and/or photoelectrochemical activities.

the polarization induced interfacially confined band bending can be used to tune the charge transport in heterogeneous photocatalyst system, which can lead to enhanced photocatalytic and/or photoelectrochemical activities.
the ferroelectric materials can serve as a new class of photocatalysts for PC and PEC hydrogen production.
